summary: Created PlayerView.axaml and PlayerView.axaml.cs implementing the video player UserControl. The view embeds a LibVLCSharp.Avalonia VideoView with MediaPlayer binding, a progress Slider with millisecond time labels (via MsToTimeConverter), a playback toolbar (Play/Pause ToggleButton, Mute ToggleButton, Volume Slider, Screenshot Button), precision seek sliders with code-behind PointerReleased handlers, and a manual seek TextBox with Enter-key handling. Fixed two XAML errors: (1) VideoView does not have a Background property — removed it; (2) CommunityToolkit.Mvvm strips the Async suffix when generating command names so ScreenshotAsync generates ScreenshotCommand, not ScreenshotAsyncCommand. Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

comments.note: VideoView from LibVLCSharp.Avalonia does not expose Background as an AvaloniaProperty, so the black background that is typical for a video player surface cannot be set directly in XAML on the VideoView element. The parent DockPanel provides the window background instead. Could use a Border or Panel wrapper around VideoView if a precise black background region is needed before media loads.

PlayerView.axaml.cs: PointerReleased is a routed event that bubbles up. If the Slider thumb is in a scrollable container, events might interfere. A more robust approach in the future would be to handle ValueChanged with a 'user is dragging' flag (using PointerPressed to set it), but for now the simple PointerReleased approach works correctly for the seek use case.

CommunityToolkit.Mvvm strips the Async suffix when naming commands: ScreenshotAsync generates ScreenshotCommand, not ScreenshotAsyncCommand. This is counter-intuitive and not immediately obvious from the method name. The WP spec referred to ScreenshotAsyncCommand — the spec should be corrected. A comment in PlayerViewModel.cs or the AGENTS.md should document this naming convention to prevent future mismatches.

The result is functionally equivalent. The AC item for this control is already marked met. No binding gap exists — just an implementation choice deviation from the spec description.

summary: Reviewed PlayerView.axaml and PlayerView.axaml.cs. All 9 acceptance criteria confirmed met. XAML structure is clean: DockPanel layout, VideoView correctly bound to MediaPlayer, progress slider with TwoWay binding + PointerReleased dual-mechanism (correct pattern), PlayPause/Mute ToggleButtons with OneWay IsChecked and command bindings, volume slider, screenshot button using ScreenshotCommand (CommunityToolkit Async-strip naming correctly applied), precision seek sliders with re-entrant-safe reset flags, manual seek TextBox with Enter-key handler. Code-behind is justified and minimal. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: PlayerView.axaml.cs OnSeekTextBoxKeyDown (line 107): SeekTextBox.Text = string.Empty and e.Handled = true execute unconditionally after the long.TryParse succeeds, even when vm.SeekCommand.CanExecute(positionMs) returns false (e.g. no media loaded). Result: the user's input is silently cleared with no feedback. Consider wrapping the clear+handled lines inside the CanExecute block, or leaving the TextBox populated and providing visual error feedback when the command is unavailable.

[documentation-forward] CommunityToolkit.Mvvm strips the 'Async' suffix from command names: ScreenshotAsync generates ScreenshotCommand, not ScreenshotAsyncCommand. The WP spec used ScreenshotAsyncCommand, which caused developer confusion. This naming convention should be documented in AGENTS.md (or as an XML doc comment on the affected VM methods) so future contributors know what name to bind in XAML. This is a cross-cutting convention that will recur in every async command.

[documentation-forward] PlayerView.axaml.cs: MsToTimeConverter is a static readonly IValueConverter defined directly on the PlayerView class and referenced from XAML via {x:Static views:PlayerView.MsToTimeConverter}. This is pragmatic but ties the converter to the View class, preventing reuse in other views without importing PlayerView. If millisecond-to-time formatting is needed elsewhere, a shared Converters static class would be appropriate. Document the current approach in AGENTS.md or a code comment so future contributors know this is an intentional design choice.

PlayerView.axaml ToggleButton (Play/Pause): Uses a Panel with two TextBlock children (IsVisible='{Binding IsPlaying}' / IsVisible='{Binding !IsPlaying}') to toggle between ⏸ and ▶ glyphs. This works correctly but is slightly verbose for a two-state toggle. A future cleanup could use a DataTrigger or style with TargetType to reduce XAML nesting. Not a blocking concern.

PlayerView.axaml ProgressSlider uses both Value='{Binding PositionMs, Mode=TwoWay}' and PointerReleased='OnProgressSliderReleased'. This dual-mechanism pattern (TwoWay keeps slider in sync during playback; PointerReleased commits the seek on drag-end) is the standard Avalonia/WPF approach for media progress controls. Architecture confirmed correct.

PlayerView.axaml.cs: Precision seek reset flags (_seekBackResetting, _seekForwardResetting) with try/finally correctly prevent re-entrant PointerReleased events when programmatically resetting slider values to 0. Clean and correct pattern for this use case.

comments.note: OnSeekTextBoxKeyDown clears SeekTextBox.Text and sets e.Handled = true unconditionally after a successful parse, even when vm.SeekCommand.CanExecute(positionMs) returns false. This means user input is silently discarded with no feedback when media is not loaded. Documented the current behaviour in api-surface.md. A future improvement should move the clear+handled lines inside the CanExecute guard for better UX.
